narrative.summary: The African Union's Executive Council endorsed the Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy and the African Digital Compact, which has a dedicated AI pillar, in July 2024, and asked Member States to support their implementation and take part in global AI governance talks. The Peace and Security Council has adopted communiqués on AI and peace, security and governance. The African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights adopted a 2021 resolution on AI and human rights and published a draft study on the subject for comment in 2025.

instruments.official_title: Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy: Harnessing AI for Africa's Development and Prosperity
instruments.issuing_authority: African Union Commission; endorsed by the Executive Council
instruments.publisher_name: African Union Commission; endorsed by the Executive Council
instruments.current_status: Endorsed by the AU Executive Council at its 45th Ordinary Session (Accra, 18-19 July 2024) in Decision EX.CL/Dec.1268(XLV), which requests Member States to support its implementation.
instruments.summary: Continental strategy for an Africa-centric, development-focused approach to AI. It sets focus areas on maximising AI benefits, building capabilities, addressing risks, inclusive governance and regulation, regional and international cooperation, and investment, with an implementation section and a call for a five-year implementation plan.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing strategy & action plans, responsible ai & ethics.

instruments.issuing_authority: African Union Commission; endorsed by the Executive Council
instruments.publisher_name: African Union Commission; endorsed by the Executive Council
instruments.summary: Africa's common vision for digital transformation, anchored in Agenda 2063 and the Digital Transformation Strategy. Pillar Eight, 'Development and Adoption of Artificial Intelligence', sets policy interventions to strengthen AI governance (regulations, standards, codes of conduct, risk-based regulation, national and regional oversight bodies), optimise AI benefits, build AI capabilities, address AI risks and threats, foster investment, and promote regional and international cooperation on AI governance.
instruments.current_status: Adopted at the 45th Ordinary Session of the AU Executive Council (Accra, Ghana, 18-19 July 2024) as Africa's common position on digital transformation; published by the AU Commission on 9 August 2024.

Endorsement verified in EX.CL/Dec.1268(XLV) para 28. | Independent check 2026-10-21: corrected from the official source.

instruments.official_title: Decision on the Reports of the Specialised Technical Committees (STCs), EX.CL/Dec.1268(XLV) - Section on the 2nd Extraordinary Session of the STC on Communication and ICT
instruments.english_title: Executive Council Decision EX.CL/Dec.1268(XLV) endorsing the African Digital Compact and the Continental AI Strategy
instruments.issuing_authority: Executive Council of the African Union
instruments.publisher_name: Executive Council of the African Union
instruments.summary: In this decision the Executive Council endorses the African Digital Compact and the Continental AI Strategy. It asks Member States to support their implementation, to have their UN missions advocate the Compact's recommendations in Global Digital Compact talks, and to take part actively in global AI governance negotiations. It asks the AU Commission to hold an African conference on AI in 2025, develop sector AI strategies, and submit both texts to the UN Secretary-General, and calls on financing institutions to mobilise resources.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Executive Council at its 45th Ordinary Session, Accra, Ghana, 18-19 July 2024 (paragraphs 28-31 of the decision).
instruments.evidence_reference: Decision covers several STC reports; the AI content is a dedicated section (paras 28-31). Session printed as 18-19 July 2024; AU decisions page dated July 18, 2024. legal_status chosen as the nearest value; the decision itself does not state its legal effect. Could be merged into the Strategy record's status instead of a separate record if editors prefer.

instruments.official_title: Communiqué of the 1267th Meeting of the Peace and Security Council, held on 20 March 2025, on Artificial Intelligence and its Impact on Peace, Security and Governance in Africa
instruments.english_title: Peace and Security Council communiqué on Artificial Intelligence and its Impact on Peace, Security and Governance in Africa (1267th meeting)
instruments.issuing_authority: Peace and Security Council of the African Union
instruments.publisher_name: Peace and Security Council of the African Union
instruments.summary: Ministerial-level communiqué on AI and peace, security and governance. It notes the creation of an Advisory Group on AI, asks the Commission to build AI-based early warning systems and to develop an African Common Position on AI, encourages an African regulatory framework on AI and security and an African charter on AI, calls for an African AI centre of excellence, an AU watch centre on AI and an African fund for AI, and encourages national AI strategies and legislation.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Peace and Security Council at its 1267th meeting, held at ministerial level on 20 March 2025.
instruments.evidence_reference: Full text read on the AU Library page (library.au.int). Communiqué reference number not shown on that page (likely PSC/MIN/COMM.1267 (2025)). Also on africanlii.org (not official). | Independent check 2026-10-21: corrected from the official source.

instruments.official_title: Resolution on the need to undertake a Study on human and peoples' rights and artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and other new and emerging technologies in Africa - ACHPR/Res. 473 (EXT.OS/XXXI) 2021
instruments.english_title: Resolution 473 on the need to undertake a study on human and peoples' rights and AI, robotics and other new and emerging technologies in Africa
instruments.issuing_authority: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
instruments.publisher_name: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
instruments.summary: Resolution calling on States Parties to ensure that AI, robotics and other new technologies comply with the African Charter and human rights standards, including dignity, privacy, equality, transparency and accountability; to work toward a comprehensive legal and ethical governance framework; and to keep AI systems with far-reaching consequences under meaningful human control. It calls on the AU and regional bodies to prioritise a regional regulatory framework and commits the Commission to a study on AI and human rights in Africa.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights at its 31st Extraordinary Session, held virtually, on 25 February 2021.
instruments.evidence_reference: Text ends 'Done virtually, on 25 February 2021'; ACHPR page lists Mar 10, 2021 (posting date). The ACHPR is a treaty body of independent commissioners, not a body of member-state representatives; legal_status set to nearest value.

instruments.summary: Draft study mandated by Resolution 473 (ACHPR/Res. 473 (EXT.OS/XXXI) 2021) on how AI, robotics and other new and emerging technologies affect human and peoples' rights in Africa. It draws on literature review, stakeholder consultations, and doctrinal, socio-legal and comparative research, and includes recommendations.
